description: Workout-tracking app with 20M+ downloads and a 4.8 App Store rating. Its own affiliate program is built for creators and coaches and pays 30% of every new subscriber's first payment, with an explicit no-cap policy, a personal code/link, and 10% off yearly Elite plans for followers.

evidence.summary: Official affiliate page: 'Share Jefit with your audience and earn 30% of every new subscriber's first payment. No cap on what you can make.' The FAQ answers 'How much can I earn?' with '30% of every new subscriber's first payment. There's no cap, so the more people you bring in, the more you earn.'

Program mechanics on the official page: affiliates get their own code and je.fit link; attribution covers a new subscriber's first payment within 90 days; followers get 10% off a yearly Jefit Elite subscription; payouts are monthly once earnings reach $15, by PayPal, bank transfer or gift card (Venmo in the US).

The page is addressed to creators, coaches and athletes ('For creators & coaches'); every application is reviewed and answered within 48 hours; the brand cites 20M+ downloads and App Store / Google Play ratings of 4.8 and 4.4.

name: Jefit

reasons.compensation: 30% of each new subscriber's first payment with an explicit 'There's no cap' FAQ answer; held just below maximum because commission applies to the first payment only, not renewals.
reasons.contact_access: No partnerships email is published, but applications are reviewed with a reply promised within 48 hours.
reasons.credibility: Established fitness app citing 20M+ downloads and a 4.8 App Store rating on its own program page.
reasons.niche_fit: A mainstream workout app that fitness creators can demo inside their own training content, with a follower discount on yearly plans.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open application on the brand's own page, reviewed within 48 hours.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The program is explicitly built for creators and coaches, with personal codes/links designed for videos, stories and bios; no creator counts are published, so saturation stays unknown.

description: Connected at-home boxing gym combining premium equipment with punch-tracking technology and trainer-led boxing and kickboxing workouts. Its affiliate program runs on Awin and pays 7.5% commission on subscription sign-ups with a 30-day cookie and a dedicated affiliate team.

evidence.summary: FightCamp's own Awin merchant profile: '7.5% commission on all FightCamp subscription sign ups', 30-day cookie length, text links and banners, seasonal ads and codes, incentives and bonuses, and a dedicated affiliate team; questions go to patrick@joinfightcamp.com.

The Awin profile names its target partners: 'Good affiliate partners include sites focused on: lifestyle bloggers, mommy bloggers, fitness bloggers, travel bloggers, and other related topics', and describes the punch-tracking product and workout library.

Third-party listings have cited a flat per-sale fee via another network for FightCamp, which conflicts with the Awin profile's 7.5% of subscription sign-ups; the 7.5% figure recorded here is the one on the brand's own Awin merchant profile, and no cap statement appears on either source, so the cap stays unknown.

name: FightCamp

reasons.compensation: 7.5% on subscription sign-ups via Awin; a modest rate on subscriptions only, with no cap statement published, so the cap is unknown.
reasons.contact_access: A named affiliate contact email (patrick@joinfightcamp.com) is published on the brand's Awin profile.
reasons.credibility: Established connected-fitness brand running a staffed program on Awin, a major network.
reasons.niche_fit: A demonstrable home-boxing product with tracking stats - strong material for fitness and home-gym creators.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Joinable through the Awin network profile.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The profile explicitly recruits fitness and lifestyle bloggers and offers banners, codes and bonuses; no creator counts are published, so saturation stays unknown.

description: US fitness-equipment retailer (Benicia, California) selling its own French Fitness gym gear plus other brands through FitnessSuperstore.com. Its Affiliate & Creator Partner Program pays 6% on FrenchFitness.com purchases and 4% on FitnessSuperstore.com purchases, tracked by link and personal coupon code.

evidence.summary: Official FAQ: '6% on purchases at FrenchFitness.com, 4% on purchases at FitnessSuperstore.com'; commissions are paid Net 30 by PayPal once the balance reaches $100, with a 14-day hold for returns; the page publishes the company address (457 Industrial Way, Benicia, CA 94510) and phone.

The program is named the 'Affiliate & Creator Partner Program'; its FAQ confirms multi-platform publishers (YouTube, Instagram, blogs) are eligible, partners get a unique coupon code and auto-apply link, a live dashboard and a dedicated account manager; product seeding is limited and prioritises larger channels.

Eligibility and tracking caveats on the official page: US-based partners only, 18+, manual review in typically 2-3 business days, W-9/SSN required for tax compliance. The page's cookie wording is inconsistent (30-day cookie in the benefits and FAQ, 7-day cookie in the rules section), and no earnings-cap statement is published, so the cap is unknown.

name: French Fitness

opportunity.title: French Fitness Affiliate & Creator Partner Program

reasons.compensation: 6% on the brand's own store (4% on the sister store) with high average order values on gym equipment; no cap statement is published, so the cap is unknown.
reasons.contact_access: No email is published, but partners get a dedicated account manager and the page prints a phone number and street address.
reasons.credibility: Operating US retailer with a physical California address, two storefronts and fully published program rules and tax requirements.
reasons.niche_fit: Home-gym and strength equipment is a natural review and setup-tour fit for fitness creators.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open application with manual review (2-3 business days), but US-based partners only and a $100 payout minimum.
reasons.ugc_evidence: Explicitly a creator partner program with coupon codes for on-screen use and multi-platform eligibility; no creator counts are published, so saturation stays unknown.

description: Small apparel brand run by its CEO, Daniel, selling clothing through its own store. Its Brand Ambassador program pays a Rank Journey commission starting at 3% of personal sales and rising to 10% as lifetime sales grow (ranks never reset), plus 50% of the earnings of ambassadors a member recruits, and states there is no limit on commissions.

evidence.summary: Official page, 'The Sky's the Limit' section: 'Our affiliate program has no limit to the amount of commissions you can make each day, week, or month. The only limit is how much you can share and convert.'

Rank Journey table on the official page: Rank 1 pays 3% of personal sales ($0-$999 lifetime sales), rising through 5%, 5.5%, 6%, 6.5%, 7%, 7.5% and 8% to 10% at Rank 10 ($25,000+); sales totals are never reset. Ambassadors generate links and QR codes from their affiliate account.

Recruiter bonus on the official page: 'for every referral you bring in that sales anything in our store, you earn 50% equivalent of whatever they make' - a multi-level style bonus on top of personal-sales commission, which creators should weigh before joining.

name: Revolutti

reasons.compensation: Explicit no-limit wording, but the starting rate is only 3% and the 10% top rate needs $25,000 of lifetime personal sales; the 50%-of-recruits bonus is a multi-level structure, so compensation scores mid-range.
reasons.contact_access: No email or named contact is published on the ambassador page; everything runs through the affiliate account.
reasons.credibility: A small, young, CEO-fronted apparel brand with a recruiter-bonus structure; little independent track record is published.
reasons.niche_fit: General apparel is an easy fit for fashion creators, though the brand itself is niche and little-known.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open self-serve registration from the ambassador page.
reasons.ugc_evidence: Ambassadors post generated links/QR codes on social media and get an account dashboard; no creator counts are published, so saturation stays unknown.

description: Women's quiet-luxury ready-to-wear brand founded in 2020 (polo shirts and dresses, sweatshirts, hoodies, blouses, in cotton). Its Ambassador Program pays a personalised 1-10% commission with no limit on total earnings, but earnings are credited as store credit after the return period; referrals get 10% off their first order.

evidence.summary: Official referral page: '1-10% Commission - Earn a personalized commission rate on every purchase made through your referral code. Your rate is determined based on factors such as your audience size, engagement, and the nature of our partnership', with the bullets 'No limit on total earnings' and 'Commission applies to all orders'.

Material caveat on the official page: 'Credited as store credit after return period' - ambassador earnings are paid in store credit, not cash. Because the 1-10% rate is set individually per ambassador, no single published rate settles, so commission_rate is recorded as null.

Application on the official page asks for an Instagram handle and social media following; applications are reviewed within 3 to 5 business days; referrals receive 10% off their first order, valid on all products including sale items, for new customers only.

name: NOWIHT

reasons.compensation: 'No limit on total earnings' is stated explicitly, but the rate is a personalised 1-10% set after application and earnings are paid as store credit rather than cash, so compensation scores conservatively.
reasons.contact_access: No email is published; questions go through the site's contact page and the application form.
reasons.credibility: Operating womenswear label founded in 2020 with clear program terms printed on its own page, but a small brand.
reasons.niche_fit: Quiet-luxury womenswear staples fit fashion and styling creators well, with a 10% first-order offer for their audience.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Application form on the official page, reviewed in 3-5 business days; the brand frames the program as exclusive/partnership-based.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The ambassador application is built around social following and Instagram handles; no creator counts are published, so saturation stays unknown.

description: Ratchet-belt brand founded in 2010, selling EDC, golf, casual and dress belts and custom buckles for men, women and children. Its affiliate program, applied for through AvantLink, is designed for influencer, eCommerce, golf, outdoor and fashion businesses and lists 'No cap on commissions' among its advantages; no percentage rate is published on the program page.

evidence.summary: Official affiliate page advantages list includes 'No cap on commissions' verbatim, alongside a tracking cookie, free US shipping and a 30-day return policy for uncut belts; the page states the program 'is designed to add a strong additional revenue stream to influencer, eCommerce, golf, outdoor, and fashion businesses' and its Apply Now link goes to AvantLink.

No commission percentage is published anywhere on the official program page - affiliates learn the rate inside AvantLink - so commission_rate is recorded as null rather than guessed. Terms note that application does not guarantee admittance and only approved coupons may be promoted.

Brand background on the official page: 'Nexbelt was founded in 2010 and is the leading provider of high-quality ratchet belts', with EDC, golf, casual and dress collections and custom buckles for men, women and children.

name: Nexbelt

reasons.compensation: 'No cap on commissions' is stated explicitly on the official page, but the percentage rate is not published at all, so compensation scores low until the rate is confirmed inside AvantLink.
reasons.contact_access: No email is published on the page; application and contact run through AvantLink.
reasons.credibility: Founded in 2010 and positioning itself as the leading ratchet-belt provider, running its program on the established AvantLink network.
reasons.niche_fit: A single demonstrable accessory (ratchet belts) that fits golf, EDC, outdoor and menswear-fashion creators.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Apply through the AvantLink link on the official page; admission is not guaranteed.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The program explicitly targets influencer businesses and permits promotion of approved coupons; no creator counts are published, so saturation stays unknown.

description: Everyday-carry and travel gear brand (slings, backpacks and accessories) with a global storefront. Its Brand Ambassador program pays 10% cash commission on every qualifying purchase, gives followers 15% off, includes free products and VIP access to launches, and pays commissions via PayPal; applications are open worldwide.

evidence.summary: Official ambassador page: 'As an ALPAKA Brand Ambassador, you'll enjoy exclusive perks like free products and 10% cash commission on every qualifying purchase. Oh, and your friends, family + followers will get 15% off their purchase, too!' plus VIP access to product launches.

Program mechanics on the official page: apply and receive an answer by email within 2 weeks; no geographic restriction ('You can apply from anywhere'); a PayPal account is required because 'we pay Ambassador commissions via PayPal'; ambassadors promote on social media (IG, TikTok, etc.). No earnings-cap statement is published, so the cap is unknown.

Third-party affiliate directories separately list an ALPAKA affiliate offer at 8%, which appears to be a different channel from the 10% ambassador program on the brand's own page; the 10% ambassador rate is the one recorded here.

name: ALPAKA

reasons.compensation: 10% cash commission on every qualifying purchase plus free product; no cap statement is published, so the cap is unknown.
reasons.contact_access: No email is published; contact runs through the ambassador application, answered within about 2 weeks.
reasons.credibility: Established carry-goods brand with international storefronts and a defined, PayPal-paid ambassador program.
reasons.niche_fit: Slings and backpacks are core gear for travel, EDC and tech-carry creators, with a 15% follower discount to promote.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open worldwide application on the official page.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The program is built around social promotion with free products and launch access; no creator counts are published, so saturation stays unknown.

Commission is earned once the activity takes place, with flexible payment options including bank transfer and PayPal. Program terms on the official page: 'No fees or commitments' to start; integration options include deep links, widgets and an automatic widget; partners get analytics reports and a dedicated Partner Engagement Team; the brand states 88% of partners report satisfaction. No earnings-cap statement is published, so the cap is unknown.

Third-party roundups report higher negotiated or network-specific rates for GetYourGuide (for example 7% via Awin and 8% via Travelpayouts); the 8% recorded here is the base rate on the brand's own Partner Resource Center.

name: GetYourGuide

reasons.compensation: 8% base commission per booking from the brand's own partner documentation; higher rates appear to be negotiated, and no cap statement is published, so the cap is unknown.

reasons.credibility: One of the largest global travel-experience marketplaces, with published partner documentation and an 88% partner-satisfaction claim.
